summary: Content engine is generating volume (31 pieces this week) but facing a critical bottleneck with only 13% approval rate and zero publications. With 469 unused triggers and strong source diversity, the system has raw material but needs strategic refinement to convert inputs into publishable content that aligns with quality standards.
whats_working: Strong source diversity with RSS (189) and Reddit (121) providing robust content discovery across multiple channels
Balanced content categorization showing strategic mix of pain points (11), data points (9), and questions (3) that address audience needs
Comprehensive format coverage across 14 different types ensures multi-platform readiness once approval issues are resolved
whats_not_working: Critical 13% approval rate (4 of 32) indicates major quality or relevance gaps between generated content and brand standards - needs immediate content brief refinement
Zero publications despite approved content suggests workflow breakdown between approval and publishing stages, creating inventory waste
recommended_topics: AI-powered intake automation for law firms - aligns with Emerging Channels pillar and addresses Lead Conversion focus, capitalizing on current legal tech trends
Local SEO case studies showing specific ranking improvements - data-driven content that leverages the DATA_POINT category strength while filling the performance gap
Budget allocation frameworks for multi-practice firms - addresses Paid Advertising pillar and provides actionable frameworks legal marketers actively search for
format_recommendations: Prioritize LinkedIn posts (32 ready) and stat graphics (6) for immediate publication since these formats typically have higher approval rates in B2B legal marketing
Reduce X thread and short video production until approval rate improves - focus resources on proven formats rather than spreading thin across all 14 types
timing_insights: With zero performance data available, implement tracking immediately and publish approved content on Tuesday-Thursday mornings (9-11 AM EST) when legal professionals are most active on LinkedIn
